t: #3122 Minimum Number of Operations to Satisfy Conditions
o: **Understanding the problem**: Make every column constant (all rows equal within a column) and adjacent columns different, changing cells one at a time. Since values are 0..9, making column j entirely value v costs (number of cells in column j ≠ v) — computable by counting. Then it's a shortest-path/DP over columns: dp[j][v] = min cost to fix columns 0..j with column j set to v, transitioning only between differing values. Example 3 (single column [1,2,3]): cheapest uniform value 1 costs 2 changes.
k: Cost of setting column j to value v depends only on column counts: m − (#cells equal to v).
DP over columns × 10 values with the constraint dp transition forbids u == v between neighbors; O(n·100) total.

a.i: Precompute eq[j][v] = count of rows with grid[i][j] == v. dp[j][v] = (m − eq[j][v]) + min over u ≠ v of dp[j−1][u]. Answer = min over v of dp[n−1][v].
s: Count eq[j][v] for every column and value.
For each subsequent column, dp[j][v] = m − eq[j][v] + min{dp[j−1][u] : u ≠ v}.
Return the minimum dp at the last column.
a.t: O(m·n + n·100) — counting plus the DP with constant 10×10 transitions

a.i: Same recurrence expressed top-down: solve(j, v) = cost of fixing columns j..n−1 given column j−1 uses value v. Memoization on (j, v) gives the same complexity and is often easier to derive live.
s: Define solve(j, prev): if j == n return 0.
For each v ≠ prev, candidate = (m − eq[j][v]) + solve(j + 1, v); take the min.
a.t: O(m·n + n·100) — each (column, previous-value) state solved once with 10 transitions
a.sp: O(n·10) — memo table plus recursion depth O(n)

w: **Wrap-up**: Recognize the two decoupled conditions: "column constant" localizes cost per (column, value) and "adjacent columns differ" makes it a chain DP — a template reusable for many grid-normalization problems. Pitfalls: trying to change values to arbitrary integers (unnecessary — 0..9 always suffices since costs only improve with more choices, and staying in-range is optimal), and forgetting the u ≠ v exclusion in transitions. Follow-ups: values up to 10⁹ (compress to at most m+1 relevant candidates per column), or require columns pairwise distinct.
